## Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis

This saved example is educational research support, not medical advice. It is shown only as a recovery fallback and was not generated during this session.

Treatment type: Antifibrotic medicine
Treatment: Pirfenidone
FDA status: Approved
Dose and schedule: Use only as prescribed; dosing and monitoring require clinician review.
What studies found: Trials found slower decline in forced vital capacity (FVC); this is not a cure.
Safety concern: Moderate — liver, gastrointestinal, and sun-sensitivity risks require monitoring. [FDA label](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=2e8c3537-36d7-4de5-9b5c-7a624b9a9e6e)
Risks: Nausea, rash, sun sensitivity, and liver-enzyme elevation.
Medication interactions: A clinician or pharmacist must review the full medication list.
Sources: [PubMed evidence](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24836312/)

Treatment type: Antifibrotic medicine
Treatment: Nintedanib
FDA status: Approved
Dose and schedule: Use only as prescribed; dosing and monitoring require clinician review.
What studies found: Trials found slower annual decline in forced vital capacity (FVC); this is not a cure.
Safety concern: Moderate — gastrointestinal, liver, and bleeding risks require monitoring. [FDA label](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=da1c9f37-779e-4682-816f-93d0faa4cfc9)
Risks: Diarrhea, liver-enzyme elevation, and bleeding risk.
Medication interactions: Anticoagulants and interacting medicines require clinician review.
Sources: [PubMed evidence](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24836310/)
